Data & Platforms.Paper: QRLIT (Quantum Reinforcement Learning for Database Index Tuning)
Data & Platforms.Data/Benchmarks: TPC-H workload; initial DB size 10 MB, sizes {10, 20, 30, 40, 70, 100} MB
Data & Platforms.Platforms/Tools: MySQL as DBMS; QGen for workload generation; Qiskit quantum simulator; Docker; macOS (MacBook Pro, Apple M1 Pro) with Ubuntu 22.04; GitHub repository

Data & Platforms.Data/Benchmarks: Real-world multisource data streams (Intel Lab, Microtremor in Delta region, AMPds2); synthetic 5/4-group correlated streams with injected outliers
Data & Platforms.Platforms/Tools: Python 3; single-pass online PCA (DBPCA); incremental online KMeans; linear SVM with SGD; GitHub repository
Apache Spark (Scala) on Kubernetes (serverless) and virtual machines (serverful); MinIO for object storage; Prometheus; Grafana; Spark History Server; Dell iDRAC/OpenManage for energy measurement

Data & Platforms.Platforms/Tools: Python-based experiments; publicly available GitHub resources; models include linear regression and DNN variants across datasets

Application Areas: Database systems optimization via AI/ML (index tuning in DB systems)
Real-time streaming analytics and explainability (EXOS-style explanations in data streams)
Cloud-native vs traditional serverful deployments for analytics workloads (GUESS evaluation)
Energy-efficient data center and edge deployments (serverless/serverful comparisons, energy instrumentation)
Robust federated learning under non-IID data and poisoning attacks (RBF defense)
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Hybridizing emerging computing paradigms (quantum computing) with established ML workflows to accelerate convergence and performance in practical tasks (QRLIT)
Real-time, memory-bounded streaming analytics with interpretable explanations (EXOS-like approach to outlier attribute explanations)
empirical, reproducible evaluation of energy-performance trade-offs in cloud-native deployments (GUESS and serverless/serverful studies)
Security-focused ML research that rigorously compares defense mechanisms under realistic non-IID data and adversarial models (RBF vs KPCA+KMeans vs LoMar)
System-oriented AI research emphasizing deployment realities, workload benchmarks, and hardware-energy instrumentation
Summary Description: Dr. Le Gruenwald's research portfolio spans quantum-assisted machine learning for database optimization, streaming data explainability and real-time analytics, and energy-aware, cloud-native evaluation of analytics workloads. His work consistently blends theoretical innovations (quantum–classical RL, online PCA, robust FL defenses) with practical system benchmarks (TPC-H/TPC-DS workloads, serverless/serverful Spark, real energy measurements) to address end-to-end performance, scalability, and security in real-world settings. Across these works, he emphasizes reproducibility, benchmark-driven evaluation, and the integration of AI methods into complex data-management and distributed-system contexts, including IoT, smart-city scenarios, and data-center operations.
